title: Chapter 251: Black Package
html:
While waiting at a red light, Uncle Zhang checked the message in the drivers’ chat group. He had just dropped Chen Ge near Huai Hua Street after listening to ghost stories for the entire journey, and fear still made his heart quiver.

“The car has a dashboard camera, GPS tracking, and a security partition. I should be fine.” He spoke loudly enough for the passenger in the back to hear while typing his reply.

“The nights have been dangerous lately. Be careful.”

“Okay.”

The light turned green. Uncle Zhang set down his phone and drove on. Buildings flashed past, and the traffic steadily thinned. He stole a glance at the passenger in the back. The man was of modest height and wore a black jacket over a faded red T-shirt.

He had entered the taxi in a hurry and said nothing beyond providing an address. Strangest of all, he kept both jacket and hood on inside the car. From the driver’s angle, only half his face was visible.

“Brother, night-shift drivers have certain unwritten rules. Normally, we avoid places like that.” Nervousness made Uncle Zhang ramble. “But since you’re already in my car, I won’t throw you out. I can only take you close to the address, though. You’ll have to walk the final hundred or two hundred meters. Is that acceptable?”

He had behaved the same way during his first journey with Chen Ge. Timid by nature, he began planning his escape before they reached the destination. The moment his passenger left the car, he would turn around and drive away.

“No. I only need to collect something. I live in the city.” The man raised his head, and his voice sounded perfectly normal. “If you leave, I’ll be stranded at the crematorium. How am I supposed to return? Do taxis visit crematoriums at night?”

Uncle Zhang considered the argument and had to concede the passenger’s point.

“If you drive me there and then drive me back, that’ll earn you two rounds of payment; won’t you earn more compared to driving back with an empty car?”

The passenger gradually persuaded him. Why give up an additional fare?

Before meeting Chen Ge, he would have agreed readily. Now he was far more cautious. “All right, but I’ll wait at the end of the road. Come back there after you collect your things.”

“Fine, as long as you don’t mind waiting.” The passenger placed his hands in his pockets, looking entirely harmless.

Apart from keeping his hood up, he sounds perfectly normal—certainly more normal than the fellow who went on a date at an abandoned school.Uncle Zhang grumbled inwardly. Jiujiang had countless night-shift taxis; why did the strange passengers always find his?

Encountering the same lunatic twice was already extraordinarily unlikely. Surely his luck had to improve now. Uncle Zhang did his best to reassure himself, though sweat still slicked his grip on the steering wheel.

Driving quickly, he reached the crematorium on the outskirts within ten minutes. Pedestrians vanished, as did the neon glow of storefronts. Only his taxi moved along the deserted road.

“We’re about there.”

Uncle Zhang kept glancing at the passenger, who had remained perfectly still throughout the journey.

“A little farther, please. You don’t need to stop at the entrance—just continue a short distance.” The passenger’s voice had grown strangely raspy, as though he inhaled between every word.

There was no light in the surrounding hundred meters, and the place was eerily quiet. The taxi moved slowly on the road like a moving black coffin.

“You can stop here.” Night air slipped through the cracked window while Uncle Zhang’s hands trembled on the wheel.

“Okay, give me two minutes.”

“Wait, the fare!”

“I’ll come back to pay you,” the passenger said lightly. There was something different about his voice.

“You...” Uncle Zhang considered getting out and demanding payment, afraid the passenger might disappear without paying. But he could not bring himself to leave the car. Who visits a crematorium at midnight? Does he work here?

Uncle Zhang checked the time: 11:56 p.m.

Keep running into these weird customers who want to come to these places. The only good thing is that I don’t need to worry about traffic.

He watched the man run away with an awkward gait, as though unaccustomed to walking. The passenger entered through a side door. Left alone, Uncle Zhang closed every window, drawing comfort from the enclosed car.

He’s taking too long.After only ten seconds, Uncle Zhang grew restless. Is he cheating me? What if he never comes back?

Then his expression changed as a dreadful realization struck him. The passenger I dropped near Huai Hua Street didn’t pay either!

Uncle Zhang had forced Chen Ge out fifty meters from Huai Hua Street and refused to advance another inch. By the time Chen Ge tried to pay, the taxi was already speeding away.

He lightly slapped his cheeks. I started work an hour ago, earned nothing, and paid for the fuel myself. Still, a few banknotes are a small price if I never see that man again.

Flustered, Uncle Zhang switched on the radio for distraction, but the music only worsened his nerves. Beyond the windows, the crematorium stood dark and silent. Noise inside the car made him feel watched. Before the song ended, he turned it off and scanned his surroundings, gripping the wheel.

Why isn’t he back yet?

It was one minute to midnight. Uncle Zhang could not shake the conviction that something terrible was about to happen. He picked up the torn talisman, muttered several prayers, and tucked it back inside his shirt.

By chance, lowering his head for the talisman brought the back seat into view. Uncle Zhang had placed a white cushion there for passengers’ comfort. An inconspicuous bloodstain now marked it.

Was this there before? I was sure this wasn’t there when I started the trip tonight.

He turned toward the rear, remembering the passenger’s strange clothing. Beneath the black jacket had been a faded red T-shirt.

The red on that shirt wasn’t even, could that be…

Bang! Bang bang!

Someone knocked on the window. The passenger had returned, carrying a package wrapped in black cloth. Startled, Uncle Zhang snapped his gaze forward.

“Found the thing, let’s go back to the city.” The passenger’s tone was completely different from before. Something had changed.

Uncle Zhang studied the package in the rearview mirror, then wiped his sweat-soaked palms against his shirt.
